description: Gonocephalus kuhlii is a species of lizard in the family Agamidae, endemic to Java, Indonesia, with an unconfirmed record from Sumatra. Originally described by German zoologist Hermann Schlegel in 1851 as Lophyrus kuhlii and named in honor of German ornithologist Heinrich Kuhl. It is diurnal and arboreal, spending most of its life on tree trunks and vegetation in humid forest habitats. An oviparous species laying clutches of four eggs. Classified as Vulnerable on the IUCN Red List (assessed 2021) due to ongoing habitat destruction from deforestation and agricultural expansion. Its taxonomic validity was confirmed in recent studies on the systematics of the genus Gonocephalus.
population_estimate: Population status unknown but considered uncommon and localized. Populations are severely fragmented due to habitat loss across its range in Java. Trend is unknown but suspected to be declining. The species is confined to remaining forest fragments, primarily in protected areas.
habitat: Primary habitat is humid montane rainforest at altitudes of 700-1,200 m above sea level on the island of Java, Indonesia. It is strictly arboreal, found on tree trunks and vegetation in the forest canopy. Requires dense, undisturbed forest habitat with high humidity levels. Known from protected areas including Ujung Kulon National Park and Gunung Halimun Salak National Park.
threats: Habitat loss due to deforestation and agricultural expansion across Java
Climate change affecting montane forest ecosystems at higher elevations
Potential collection for the pet trade
Limited range restricted to high-elevation forests on a single island
Conversion of forest to plantations and human settlements
ecosystem_role: As an arboreal insectivore, helps control populations of insects, spiders, and other arthropods in the forest canopy. Serves as both predator and prey in the montane forest ecosystem. Contributes to the ecological balance of Java's remaining rainforest canopies. The species' dependence on undisturbed forest makes it a potential indicator species for forest health.
human_connection: Named after German ornithologist Heinrich Kuhl (1796-1821), who contributed significantly to the early natural history exploration of Indonesia. First described by Schlegel in 1851 from specimens collected in Java. Holds scientific significance in taxonomic studies of the genus Gonocephalus. The species' restricted range and specialized habitat make it a conservation priority for Java's remaining forests.

fun_fact: Named after Heinrich Kuhl, a German naturalist who explored Indonesia but died of a tropical disease at age 25
The genus name Gonocephalus means 'angle-headed' in Greek, referring to its distinctive triangular head shape
Part of a group of lizards known as 'angle-headed dragons' for their unusual head morphology
The species was first described in 1851 and its validity was confirmed only in recent genetic studies
Females lay clutches of exactly four eggs, suggesting a fixed clutch size unlike many other agamids
